title: How I built and launched Hoard Your Ground with ChatGPT 6.1 and 6 Astra
author: Gal_sh3
selftext:
I’ve released my mobile game, Hoard Your Ground, on Android and iPhone. I used ChatGPT 6 Astra and 6.1 Sol throughout development: writing and debugging code, creating graphics and sound, and helping build the ads, in-app purchases and trailer.



The game is a portrait, three-lane dragon survival game. Fire is automatic; you change lanes, time tail-sweep counters and build up a Roar. The finished game also includes four bosses, endless progression, a 90-second Daily Siege and cosmetic collector dragons.



My workflow was a lot of back-and-forth: describing what I wanted, trying the result in the game, then working through changes with ChatGPT. Getting combat, touch controls, visuals, audio and the store integrations into one playable release took repeated testing and adjustment. The collector-dragon purchases change appearance, not combat strength.



I’ve included the existing trailer, screenshots of the two live store listings and a gameplay image already used in the listing. The game is free to download, with optional rewarded ads and cosmetic purchases.



Android and iPhone: [https://solo.to/hoardyourground](https://solo.to/hoardyourground)



I’m the developer, and I’m happy to discuss the process. Which part of taking an AI-assisted mobile game to release would you most want to see broken down?
